Application Materials.content:
Applicants must submit the following documents through the [Online Application System](https://www.gradsch.cuhk.edu.hk/OnlineApp/login_email.aspx) by the specified deadline:
- Academic/Professional Certificates: For all applicants, both graduation and professional qualification certificates. For degrees obtained from Chinese Mainland: both degree (學位證書) and graduation (畢業證書) certificates printed in Chinese; a valid Online Verification Reports of Higher Education Qualification Certificates (教育部學歷證書電子註冊備案表) and Degree Certificates (中國高等教育學位在線驗證報告) issued from CHESICC for Mainland China degrees.
- Official Transcripts and Grading Schemes - Application Stage: All copies of official transcripts and grading schemes with explanatory notes for all tertiary education. E-transcripts must be sent directly by the issuing university, paper transcripts must be in a sealed envelope issued by the university. Transcripts must bear official seal; unofficial or improper letterhead documents will not be accepted. Non-English/Chinese transcripts require certified English translation. CUHK graduates can submit photocopies of transcripts (excluding CUHK (Shenzhen)); the University reserves the right to require an original copy.
- **The University requires applicants to provide verification reports of the qualification obtained. Applicants will be notified by the Graduate Division concerned/Graduate School separately.**
- English Language Proficiency Requirements: Submit one of the following: a copy of graduation certificate issued by a university in Hong Kong; a certifying letter issued by the Registry of the university confirming the medium of instruction of your degree programme was English; an official score report of TOEFL, IELTS (Academic), or GMAT (Verbal); Certification of Results of the English Language subject in Hong Kong Advanced Level Examination (AS Level), Hong Kong Higher Level Examination, or Hong Kong Diploma of Secondary Education Examination provided by Hong Kong Examinations and Assessment Authority; certified true copy of Statement of Results/report of the English Language subject in GCE A-level or AS-level/CUHK Matriculation Examination; or certified true copy of a recognised Professional Qualifications certificate where the examination was in English.
- Confidential Recommendations: Other programmes: **Two referee reports are required**. Submit referee information via [Online Application System](https://www.gradsch.cuhk.edu.hk/OnlineApp/login_email.aspx).
- Identification Documents: Hong Kong Identity Card or other identity document.
- Qualification Assessment (HKCAAVQ): Degrees awarded by overseas universities by distance learning or by completing a curriculum of short duration may be required to provide [HKCAAVQ](https://www.hkcaavq.edu.hk/en/) assessment on the level of qualification obtained. Applicants will be notified by the Graduate Division concerned separately.
- **Applicants will be required to complete an Authorisation Form for the University to verify their academic qualifications. The programme staff may further contact the applicants to proceed with applying for academic verification from a third-party organization, e.g., Chinese Service Center for Scholarly Exchange (CSCSE) as needed.**
- Submitted documents are non-returnable; materials from unsuccessful applications will be destroyed after the completion of the admission exercise.

Application Deadlines.content: MSc in Risk Management Science and Data Analytics: Priority round: **31 December 2025**; Final round: **28 February 2026**. Applications will be processed on a rolling basis until all places have been filled. Early applications are strongly encouraged.

Academic Requirements.content:
- Applicants should **hold a Bachelor’s degree with Second Honours Class or above in Business, Science, Finance, Economics, Engineering or related disciplines**.
- Applicants should **preferably possess knowledge of Business, Economics and/or Finance though not compulsory**.
- The programme expects candidates to have **a general background in mathematics and statistics**; in particular, candidates are expected to be familiar with **calculus, linear algebra, probability and statistical inference at the junior undergraduate level**.
- **Proficiency in computer programming is a plus**.

GRE GMAT Requirements.content: The GRE is not required, but you may choose to submit the report as supplementary information.

Program Overview.content:
Risk management is an important subject in both the financial and public sectors. A successful risk management system incorporates expert knowledge from mathematics, statistics, actuarial science, finance, computing and engineering. The Risk Management Science programmes offered by the Department of Statistics and Data Science at The Chinese University of Hong Kong have played leading roles in the development of the risk management discipline in Hong Kong. The highly successful Master of Science Programme in Risk Management Science was launched in 2003 and was renamed M.Sc. in Risk Management Science and Data Analytics in 2021-22 to reflect the new elements of the evolving field of data analytics. Graduates are equipped with state-of-the-art risk management expertise that will allow them to play a leading role in the industry.
- Study mode: Full-time (1 year) or Part-time (2 years).
- Lecture format: Each course consists of a three-hour lecture each week.
- Time and venue: Weekday evenings and Saturdays at CUHK in Shatin.
- Programme structure: Students are required to complete a minimum of 24 credits in order to graduate. The full-time mode normally lasts one year, with core and elective courses across two semesters. The part-time mode normally lasts two years, with core and elective courses across the first and second years.
- Academic partnership: The M.Sc. in Risk Management Science and Data Analytics programme is an Academic Partner of the Global Association of Risk Professionals (GARP). GARP describes the programme as highly rigorous and interdisciplinary, providing students with a solid grounding in mathematics, finance, statistics and related areas, positioning them to pursue the FRM designation and assume strategic roles within the global risk management profession.
- Accreditation: The M.Sc. in Risk Management Science and Data Analytics has been accredited by the Royal Statistical Society (RSS). Graduates may apply for Graduate Statistician status with the RSS, subject to a satisfactory combination of modules completed. The accreditation covers the 2023-24 intake through the 2028-29 intake.
- Experiential learning: The practicum provides a bridge between the classroom and the real business world. Students complete a project assigned by a company or organization on a part-time basis under the joint supervision of an instructor and a member of the company or organization, then give a final project presentation and submit a written report.
- Career support: The programme provides workshops on CV writing and interview skills, career talks and company visits to support students’ career development. Activities mentioned include interview skills and assessment centre workshops, CV writing and individual CV editing, career talks by the Census and Statistics Department of the HKSAR Government and on cryptocurrency, and company visits to Bloomberg L.P. Hong Kong Office, Natixis, and the Census and Statistics Department.
- Facilities and industry-related learning: The Department of Statistics provides state-of-the-art computing facilities for teaching and research, including a computer laboratory with Microsoft 365/Office 2016 Professional Plus, MATLAB, R, SAS and IBM SPSS Statistics, and Bloomberg Terminals providing real-time financial data and news. NVIDIA Deep Learning Institute workshops were organized, giving students a chance to apply GPU-accelerated machine learning algorithms and receive an electronic NVIDIA DLI certificate after passing the assessment.
- Faculty and teaching staff include Dr Wong Tat Wing, Director of the MSc RMDA programme and Lecturer at CUHK’s Department of Statistics, who holds Associate of the Society of Actuaries and Financial Risk Manager designations and is a Certified Instructor and University Ambassador at the NVIDIA Deep Learning Institute; Dr Cheung King Chau, Deputy Director of the MSc RMDA programme and Lecturer, whose research interests are in network and financial data and portfolio management; Professor Wong Hoi Ying, Professor of Statistics, Outstanding Fellow of the Faculty of Science, and Associate Dean of Science (Student Affairs), whose research focuses on mathematical finance, actuarial science, FinTech, and machine learning; Professor Zhang Jiacheng, Assistant Professor in the Department of Statistics, whose research focuses on probability theory, stochastic optimization, stochastic partial differential equations, partial differential equations, mathematical finance, stochastic portfolio theory and stochastic volatility modeling; Dr John Alexander Wright, Senior Lecturer whose research interests lie in applied probability, especially financial mathematics, and who holds FRM and Professional Risk Manager designations; and Professor Yau Chun Yip, Professor in the Department of Statistics, whose research interests include financial time series, change-point analysis, and extreme value theory.
- Guest lecturers include Juan Lago, Managing Director and Chief Representative Asia-Pacific at Banco Security, with 18 years of finance experience in Madrid, New York, Chile and Hong Kong; Dr Joaquin Calvo, with more than 20 years of financial industry experience in consulting and major financial institutions across APAC, Europe and the Americas, including service as Head of Market Risk and Liquidity at a bank in Hong Kong; Franco Leung, Director, Market Outreach at S&P Global Ratings, with over 20 years of experience in credit analysis, corporate rating and research, corporate treasury, fixed income markets, risk governance and portfolio risk management; and Terrence Ho, who shares 30 years of trading experience.
- Alumni outcomes and perspectives include graduates working as a pilot at Cathay Pacific, an Operational Risk Management Specialist at an international bank, Director of Risk Consulting at KPMG Advisory (HK) Limited, Fitch Ratings, Data and Information Management at HSBC Insurance Asia Limited, PhD studies in Informatics at Nagoya University, Business Analyst at NumeriX LLC, The Bank of East Asia, and Nanyang Commercial Bank. Alumni describe the programme as balancing theoretical and practical learning, offering small-class teaching, flexible and well-structured study, practical programming skills, exposure to practitioners, project-based assignments, company visits, workshops, guest lectures, job opening referrals, and preparation for careers in risk management, banking, insurance, FinTech, consulting and further research.

Curriculum.content:
Study format: Full-time (1 year) or Part-time (2 years). Each course consists of a three-hour lecture each week. Time & venue: weekday evenings & Saturdays at CUHK in Shatin.
Students are required to complete a minimum of **24 credits** in order to graduate. Students should take at least 2 elective courses at RMSC6000 level or above, or at STAT5000 level or above.
Part-time mode: the normative study period is two years. Students should satisfy the following requirements:
- 1st Year: Core courses: 6 credits; Elective courses: 6 credits
- 2nd Year: Core courses: 6 credits; Elective courses: 6 credits
- Total: **24 credits**
Suggested study plan for part-time mode:
- 1st Term of Year 1: RMSC5002, RMSC5101, RMSC6003
- 2nd Term of Year 1: RMSC5004, RMSC5102, STAT6105, STAT6104
- 1st Term of Year 2: RMSC5003, RMSC6002, STAT5103
- 2nd Term of Year 2: RMSC5001, RMSC6001, RMSC6007, STAT6209
Full-time mode: the normative study period is one year. Students should satisfy the following requirements:
- 1st Semester: Core courses: 6 credits; Elective courses: 6 credits
- 2nd Semester: Core courses: 6 credits; Elective courses: 6 credits
- Total: **24 credits**
Suggested study plan for full-time mode:
- 1st Term of Year 1: RMSC5002, RMSC5003, RMSC5101, RMSC6002, RMSC6003, STAT5103
- 2nd Term of Year 1: RMSC5001, RMSC5004, RMSC5102, RMSC6001, RMSC6007, RMSC6008, STAT5105, STAT6104, STAT6105, STAT6204, STAT6209
Core courses:
- RMSC 5001 Advanced Statistical Theory in Risk Management: modern applications of advanced statistical methods in finance, including Monte Carlo simulation, EWMA and GARCH model, Value at Risk, and data mining methods.
- RMSC 5002 Principles of Risk Management: fundamental concepts of risk and risk management, and risk management tools used in financial products.
- RMSC 5003 Risk Measures: methodologies of calculating Value-at-Risk (VaR), including historical simulation, parametric VaR, delta-gamma approximation and Monte-Carlo simulation.
- RMSC 5004 Cases for Risk Management in Practice / Special Topics in Risk Management: students need to present and discuss literatures assigned to them by the instructor on topics of current interest in financial risk management.
Elective courses:
- RMSC 5101 Statistical Methods in Risk Management and Finance
- RMSC 5102 Simulation Techniques in Risk Management and Finance
- RMSC 6001 Interest Rates and Fixed Incomes Risk Management
- RMSC 6002 Credit Risk Management
- RMSC 6003 Risk Management in Financial Institutions
- RMSC 6006 Portfolio Theory with Risk Management Perspective
- RMSC 6007 Risk and Financial Data Analytics with Python
- RMSC 6008 Practicum: students will be required to complete a project assigned by a company or an organization on a part-time basis, under the joint supervision of an instructor and a member of the company or organization; students will give a final project presentation and submit a written report.
- STAT 5103 High-Dimensional Data Analysis
- STAT 5105 Applied Survival Data Analysis
- STAT 6104 Financial Time Series
- STAT 6105 Basic Actuarial Principles and Their Applications
- STAT 6204 Advanced Time Series
- STAT 6209 Special Topics in Statistics
Other university requirements: students must fulfill the Term Assessment Requirement of the Graduate School, and a student must achieve a cumulative grade point average (GPA) of at least **2.0** in order to graduate.
Course exemption: students who passed FRM Part 1 Exam are eligible for exemption of core course RMSC5002 Principles of Risk Management. Only the course but not the units are exempted. Students who are exempted RMSC5002 must complete another 3-unit course to fulfil the graduation requirements.

Financial Aid.content:
The programme is an Academic Partner of the Global Association of Risk Professionals (GARP). FRM scholarships will be awarded to selected full-time students. The exam registration fee for FRM Part I Exam will be waived.
RMSC5003 Risk Measures and RMSC5102 Simulation Techniques in Risk Management and Finance have been included in the list of reimbursable courses under the [Continuing Education Fund](https://www.wfsfaa.gov.hk/en/ce/cef/overview.php). The mother programme (Master of Science in Risk Management Science and Data Analytics) of these courses is recognized under the Qualifications Framework (QF Level 6).
The programme is supported by the UGC’s Hong Kong Future Talents Scholarship Scheme for Advanced Studies for the **2025–26 and 2026-27 intakes** for selected local students. Please refer to the [Hong Kong Future Talents Scholarship Scheme for advanced Studies](https://www.gs.cuhk.edu.hk/admissions/scholarships-fees/ftss) for more details.
- The main objectives of the Scheme are to attract more meritorious local students in priority areas conducive to the development of Hong Kong.
- FTSS awardees are required to pay a minimum tuition fee being the prevailing rate of the UGC-funded full-time degree programmes (i.e. HK$44,500 (for the 2025/26 intake) and HK$47,000 (for the 2026/27 intake), and the differences will be subsidised by the scholarships subject to a cap of HK$100,000 for each student for the whole taught postgraduate programme, regardless of the actual study period and mode of study.
- The scholarship will be used for the settlement of the tuition fee only.

Multiple Applications.content: You can apply for multiple programmes, but you must submit separate applications and pay the application fees for each programme. The paid application fee is non-refundable and non-transferable. If admitted to multiple programmes, you can only enrol in one. All fees paid to the previous programmes will not be refunded or transferred. The application fee is **HK$500 per programme** (except for MBA, MBA in Finance and MSc in Finance).

Deferral Admission Policy.content:
Successful applicants are normally admitted to the following Fall Term (beginning in August). Applications for deferred admission to the Spring Term (beginning in January) or the next academic year will only be considered if students are unable to take up the study due to illness or an unavoidable cause. The **maximum period for deferred admission is one year**. Applications for deferred admission should be made to the Graduate Division Head before the start of the academic year.
An applicant who has been offered admission but wishes to defer registration, i.e., deferred admission, should submit an application before the start of the academic year to the Head of the Graduate Division for approval.

Conditional Admission Policy.content:
Yes. Final-year undergraduates can apply for postgraduate programme admission; they should submit their latest official transcript and, if accepted, provide an official final transcript and degree certificate upon admission.
For an admission offer with condition(s), applicants should follow [How to Register](https://www.gs.cuhk.edu.hk/registration/how-to-register) for provisional registration. Student status is **not yet confirmed** and students will **NOT be allowed to begin studies until all specified condition(s) are fulfilled** and academic qualification is verified by the deadline in the Admission Notification.
If the applicant cannot provide document(s) to fulfil the admission condition(s) by the deadline, the admission offer will be **withdrawn**. Applicants are also required to have their academic qualifications verified before the admission date.
